configuration.note: A line layer is read from a file, taken from the border two study areas share, or drawn on a map. A drawn line needs two positions at least; one click is a place, not a route, and the refusal says so and stays on screen. At most 200 lines are drawn one by one, past which a file is the right instrument. A drawn layer carries source 'drawn' so a reader can tell an observation somebody made from a file somebody published.

ports.note: The two areas are inputs only where the layer is a border, and then both are required: the border is the stretch of the first's outline within the stated distance of the second's. Read from a file, the layer has no inputs.

ontology.note: No ontology mapping yet, and no receipt of its own: the lines are handed on as GeoJSON, and a border's source names the two areas and the distance.

changes.description: A drawn line now ends in an ARROWHEAD rather than a filled dot, pointing the way the line runs; the hollow marker at its start is unchanged. It is the same head the Map draws when its Configure dialog is set to mark direction, so the editor reads the way the figure will. Two marks for one fact was clutter, and the dot said which end was the end without saying which way the line went.

The drawing map showed one tile in a corner with grey around it. The dialog's panel has no size yet when the map is mounted, so Leaflet measured a container of nothing and asked for a single tile. It is now settled after layout and watched for every later change of size, full screen among them, as the pin editor and the georeference dialog are.

evidence.note: Unit tested: the order of clicking as the direction, reversing without redrawing, a repeated click as one position, a one-position line refused with how to continue it, names that never collide, the 200-line limit, a drawn layer reopening to be added to, and the end bearing of a line whose last segment has no length (no arrowhead, rather than one at an arbitrary angle). Browser tested on Chromium: a route drawn on the map, refused at one position, finished, named, reversed, applied and run, reaching the Map it is wired to. NOT established: that anything checks a drawn route against the ground it was drawn over, and the arrowhead's bearing is not asserted in a browser test -- it is checked in the static renderer, which computes it the same way.
